A part of the story that few mention. Professional mathematicians get huge numbers of letters from amateurs. The more well known they are, the more letters they get. Very often these letters make grand claims. Usually that the writer has proven some famous unsolved problem, or disproven an established theorem. They are full of mistakes, misunderstandings, and illogical arguments.

The letters are often discarded without being read, or quickly skimmed with great skepticism. Much like you might delete 50 spam emails in your inbox at the start of the day. Hardy giving Ramanujen's letter attention is more impressive in this light.

Regarding your remark at [15:42], you completely miss the spiritual essence of Ramanujan's decision. It wasn't about a fear of being barred from temples; for Ramanujan, every action was guided by his Ishta Devi. He didn't seek social approval; he sought divine permission. He spent three days in deep meditation until Goddess Namagiri Thayar blessed him with a vision and granted him permission to cross the seas. To reduce his profound faith to 'social fear' is a disservice to his genius.

Furthermore, you misunderstand the role of temples. In our tradition, the relationship with the Divine is private and doesn't depend on a structure at all. God isn't bound to any temple, Rather the real temple inside which we can have his "Darshan" is this living human body. Outside temples were simply built as energy centers to provide the best atmosphere for learning, meditating, mental clarity, relaxing mind and community help—not as tools for exclusion.

Sir, your understanding of the Indian social system is factually incomplete and totally distorted. The Varna system was originally based on 'Varna' (aptitude and profession) rather than birth. No one was forced into a profession; it was based on mental aptitude and hard work.

Secondly, your description of untouchability is misleading. Historically, many of these were hygiene practices, not a statement of superiority or inferiority. Just as one maintains distance when someone has a viral infection today, it wasn't about the person being 'untouchable' but about ritual and physical cleanliness.

Furthermore, Brahmins weren't 'superior'—they held a specific responsibility as teachers and scientists to shape the future. Many people born in diverse backgrounds became warriors, teachers, and scientists. I suggest checking British research on the Gurukul system, which proves that caste was never a barrier to education before the system was dismantled.

*Please do a deeper study of Indian history before promoting such generalized narratives. *

This is a method of regularisation, and I'll just explain this intuitively(and not exactly formally)

Ramanujan basically would have thought "Why these diverging series all going to infinity are not identical in looks? There must be something different about them, maybe their expressions yield different 'shadows'. And those SHADOWS are nothing but some first order terms that decide the 'Base' of a numeric result. The blowing up numbers afterwards are just residues that show us INFINITY."

Like,
Even though S=1-1+1-1+1-1+... is diverging, its shadow is 1/2
or we can say, 

S= 1/2+(higher order diverging terms that are infinite residue)

Similarly, 

S=1+2+3+...= -1/12+(infinite residue)

Similarly for harmonic series, 

S=1+1/2+1/3+...= (Euler-Mascharoni constant)+(Infinite residue)
Higher forms of mathematics are abstract; maybe Ramanujan had exceptional abstract intelligence and couldn't explain it to others or understand it himself.
